summary: Joen Imai specializes in Buddhist studies and has served as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested in 2010 and 2026.

Joerg Tuske is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as an associate professor of philosophy at Salisbury University (attested 2013).

Joey Hung works in computational and Buddhist studies. Educated at PLK Fong Wong Kam Chuen Primary School, Po Leung Kuk Centenary Li Shiu Chung Memorial College, and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, he held posts at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) studied history, archaeology, and Indology at Presidency University and Bangabasi College. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, Patna College from 1912, and became a University Reader at Patna University in 1923.
Johan Andreas dèr Mouw (1863–1919) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University between 1883 and 1887, having studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern in 1883.

Johan Elverskog is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned degrees from UC Berkeley (B.A.) and Indiana University Bloomington (M.A.), and became Dedman Family Distinguished Professor at Southern Methodist University around 2002.

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and Berlin under Antonie Rutgers and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and served as Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).

Johan Hendrik Gallée (1847–1908) studied linguistics and Indology at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later taught at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem (1872–1879) and served as a lektor at Utrecht University (1881–1892).

Johan Hendrik Kern (1867–1933) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Leiden (Ph.D. 1891), and under Eduard Sievers and August Leskien. He served on the faculties of Leiden University and the University of Groningen (1901–1924).

Johan Huizinga (1872–1945) was a historian and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. from Groningen and studied at Leipzig and Leiden under Speyer, Kern, and Uhlenbeck. He taught at Amsterdam, Groningen (1905–1915), and Leiden University (1915–1941).

Johan Nicolai Madvig (1804–1886) was a Danish linguist. Educated at Frederiksborg Gymnasium and the University of Copenhagen, he served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1829 to 1879.

Johan van Manen (1877–1943) was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He served at the Adyar Library, the National Library of India, the Indian Museum in Kolkata, and as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (1923–1939).

Johann Albrecht Bernhard von Dorn (1805–1881) studied Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological subjects at Halle and Leipzig. He served as professor at Kharkiv and the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum starting in 1842.

Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) studied at the University of Munich. He held teaching posts at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano and the Bavarian Cadet Corps, served at the Bavarian State Library, and became a professor at the University of Munich in 1828.

Johann August Vullers (1803–1880) studied Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics at Giessen, Bonn, and Halle, learning from scholars including Schlegel, Bopp, and Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Privatdozent at Bonn and Professor of Oriental Languages at Giessen from 1833.

Johann Caspar von Orelli (1787–1849) was a scholar of linguistics. He held teaching posts at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1814–1819), Carolinum Zürich (~1819–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christian Christoph Rüdiger (1751–1822) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Halle from 1768, later serving there as Privatdozent from 1777 and as extraordinary professor of Kameralwissenschaften from 1791.

Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) was a linguist who studied at Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle. He taught at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt from 1758 and became Oberbibliothekar at the Saxon State and University Library Dresden in 1787.

Johann Detloff Prochnow (1814–1888) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Greifswald (1837–1840). He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1843 and directed Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church (~1858–1883).
